1. Purpose of This Tool

This planner helps you estimate the Queries Per Minute (QPM) capacity required to deliver a great user experience for Genie for API-driven applications.

Instead of relying on simple averages or rough heuristics, this model simulates your actual traffic patterns, including:
- Daily fluctuations (morning, afternoon, global peaks)
- Session length and interaction timing
- Query behaviour (fast, standard, slow)
- Weekend vs weekday usage
- Human-driven think-time between queries

The goal is to help you choose a QPM reservation that balances:
- Performance (minimizing queueing)
- Cost efficiency (avoiding over-provisioning)
- Real-world user behaviour

2. Why This Matters

Genie and LLM-powered applications behave differently from classic BI dashboards:
- Users think, type, interpret, and iterate.
- Queries come in bursts, not evenly spaced.
- Interaction speed varies drastically between users.
- Peaks can come from multiple time zones or multiple departments.

Traditional spreadsheet formulas (average users, standard deviation) cannot capture this complexity.

This tool helps teams:
- Size QPM before adoption or rollout
- Identify when peaks exceed capacity
- Avoid user frustration caused by queueing
- Optimize cost by selecting a reservation that meets SLA needs
- Communicate QPM needs clearly to procurement or platform teams

3. How the Model Works (High-Level)

This planner combines user-provided inputs with a daily traffic simulation to compute expected demand.

Phase 1 — Base traffic assumptions

You provide:
- Average + peak users per hour
- Session duration
- Number of peaks per day
- Peak width
- Weekend scaling
- Interaction behaviour (Fast / Standard / Slow)

From these, we compute:
- Average concurrent users
- Peak concurrent users
- Avg and Peak QPM per user

Phase 2 — Daily demand modelling

The model constructs a 24-hour demand curve:
- Gaussian peaks representing load spikes
- Evenly spaced peak centers
- Adjustable peak sharpness
- Separate weekday + weekend curves

This becomes the true demand profile that reflects real behaviour.

Phase 3 — Applying your QPM reservation

You enter the QPM reservation you want to test.

The model evaluates:
- Where demand exceeds capacity
- How many queries would queue
- What percentage of the day you’re over the cap
- Average utilisation of reserved capacity

This output directly drives SLA decisions.

Phase 4 — Tradeoff Curve (Reservation vs Queueing)

The tool simulates reservation levels from 0 → 200 QPM.

For each reservation level, it computes:
- % of total queries queued
- % of time demand exceeds reservation
- Average utilisation

This produces the Queueing vs QPM Reservation curve, which shows the optimal balance between:
- Cost (QPM purchased)
- Performance (user wait times)

This is the single most important visualization for decision-making.
